why: A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric and ANY smooth curve γ in N on [0,1] (not only geodesics), the Jacobi equation is encoded WITHOUT a frame as the first-order linear system jacSys in V×V for (J, DJ/dt) (coefficients S = P'P − PP', K = R(V,P·)V); A asserts existence (the first component of the solution jacSol with tangent data at any s ∈ [0,1] is a Jacobi field, the second is its covariant derivative), that every Jacobi field is given by jacSol from its data at any s, and uniqueness from (J(s), DJ/dt(s)) for any s. B: for abstract connected Riemannian ℝⁿ-manifolds with a Levi-Civita connection and a geodesic γ on [0,1]: (i) orthonormal parallel frames along γ exist, (ii) in any such frame J = Σ fⁱPᵢ is a Jacobi field iff the fⁱ are smooth with f''ⁱ + Σⱼ c_ij fʲ = 0, c_ij = ⟨R(V,Pⱼ)V,Pᵢ⟩, (iii) Jacobi fields with the same J(0), DJ/dt(0) agree. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: abstract vs embedded setting, and even on ↥N A has no parallel frames (i) and no frame form of the equation (ii). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: setting; B has no existence statement (A's isJacobiField_jacSol), only s = 0, only geodesics, and nothing about the project's jacSol.
